assignment: M8-007-PROTOCOL-001 native HPACK Huffman wall-time validation
conclusion: The finding is not merely a speculative optimization opportunity. With the actual SDK 1.1.3 native compiler and the repository/CJPM default invocation (no explicit optimization flag), a valid 65,536-byte Huffman payload decoded synchronously in a median 5.590 s and could not observe cancellation or deadline while running. This materially validates the remotely triggerable CPU-consumption concern and supports retaining the existing release blocker. There is no frozen codec-specific latency threshold, and this isolated run did not exercise a network peer or sibling stream, so it does not quantify end-to-end amplification; formal blocker ownership/reclassification still belongs to the security gate owner.
proven: `decodeHpackHuffman` performs the reported per-bit linear exact-symbol scan and usually a second linear prefix scan over 257 entries.
The maximum valid direct-codec corpus produced correct output in every measured run; median latency was 5.590 s, range 5.442–5.879 s, n=5.

Decoding is synchronous from the HTTP/2 connection reader dispatch, and the decoder has no OperationContext, cancellation, deadline, or time/work-budget parameter/check. Closing transport or cancelling another task cannot preempt its inner CPU loop.
Compressed bytes, decoded bytes, header-list bytes, and field count are bounded; output limit +1 fails closed. Those bounds cap memory but do not make CPU cost operationally small.
The source copies compiled in scratch match the current repository sources byte-for-byte under typed text digests.
not_proven: No end-to-end network flood, multi-connection saturation, or sibling-stream responsiveness experiment was run.
No project document defines a codec-specific wall-time/work ceiling. The PRD's 50 ms cancellation P99 applies to blackhole connect, blocked read/write, and pool wait—not HPACK decode.

A full HPACK block spends a few bytes on literal/length framing, so a wire-reachable Huffman payload is a few bytes below the direct function's 65,536-byte input ceiling; this does not materially change the measured cost but should be stated in final wording.

measurement.build: cjc src/hpack_core.cj src/hpack_huffman.cj src/main.cj -o hpack_measure; matches observed `cjpm build -V` default with no explicit optimization flag
measurement.controls: CPU affinity 2; no network; per-scenario external timeout 30 or 60 seconds; warmups before recorded samples

cases.case: maximum direct compressed limit, repeated symbol 253

contracts.bounds: Http2Limits defaults: maxHeaderBlockBytes=65,536, maxHeaderListBytes=65,536, maxHeaderFields=128. HpackDecoder rejects oversized blocks before decode; decodeHpackString applies encoded and decoded ceilings; appendHuffmanByte checks before every output byte; final field accounting adds RFC table overhead.
contracts.cancellation_timing: Global request stages share a request Deadline, but HPACK decode has no context/checkpoint. The only explicit P99<=50 ms cancellation target is scoped to blackhole connect, blocked read/write, and pool wait. No HPACK-specific latency ceiling exists.
contracts.reader_impact: HTTP/2 requires one reader loop per connection; client and server invoke decoder.decode synchronously after assembling a complete header block, so decode delays all subsequent frame dispatch on that connection.

repository_mutations: None; only isolated scratch files were created.
